title: Fluid typography with clamp
when: The user wants headings and text that scale smoothly between phone and desktop instead of jumping at breakpoints.
inputs: min and max size per heading level
the viewport range, 360 to 1280 px by default
prompt:
Goal: Sizes that interpolate from a minimum at 360 px to a maximum at 1280 px with clamp, and still respond to zoom.
Steps:
1. Choose min and max per step, for example h1 from 32 px to 56 px; body stays near 1rem to 1.125rem.
2. Slope = (max - min) / (1280 - 360); the vw part is slope x 100; the intercept is min - slope x 360, written in rem.
3. Worked example for h1: slope 24 / 920 = 0.0261, so 2.61vw, intercept 22.6 px: clamp(2rem, 1.41rem + 2.61vw, 3.5rem).
4. Always mix rem with vw in the middle value so browser zoom and font settings still scale the text.
5. Store results as --step-0 to --step-5 on :root and reuse the method for section padding if wanted.
6. Check 320, 768 and 1440 px: no heading wraps one word per line.
Quality bar:
- Minimum sizes readable on phones.
- Text zooms to 200 percent.
- Headings carry the scaling, body barely changes.
Pitfalls:
- font-size: 5vw alone, which ignores zoom.
- A min larger than the max.
- Fluid body text that turns huge on wide monitors.
Verify:
- [ ] Each clamp has a rem min, rem plus vw middle and rem max.
- [ ] Values live in :root tokens.
- [ ] Nothing below 12 px at 320 px.
- [ ] Headings fit at 320 px.
Output: Fluid type tokens on :root in style.css, with the viewport range in a comment.

examples.input: titulos que diminuem suavemente no celular
